haiku-low.q1: It writes the orders row (PENDING, customer email, requestId) and an OrderPlaced outbox row in one transaction, then returns 202 with the orderId. Nothing else has acted yet.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the broker acknowledges the publish, the relay marks the row sent. If it crashes after the ack but before the mark, the row is resent on the next poll, so delivery is at-least-once.
haiku-low.q3: All of an order's events share one topic, order-events, keyed by orderId. The broker gives each partition to one instance per consumer group, so one order's events are handled in publish order.
haiku-low.q4: Only a StockReserved event triggers the charge, with key charge:orderId. Inventory emits it only after its conditional update reserves stock, so no charge happens without reserved stock.
haiku-low.q5: Each writes its result event to its own outbox in the same transaction as its state change, and its relay publishes it. If it crashes after commit, the unsent row stays in the outbox and is published on a later poll.
haiku-low.q6: Each consumer inserts the eventId into processed_events, which has a primary key. A duplicate hits that key, so the handler changes nothing, writes no outbox row and acks. Business-key guards also block repeats.
haiku-low.q7: Payment resends the same idempotency key charge:orderId on redelivery. The provider returns the first result without charging again, so Payment does not charge twice.
haiku-low.q8: A decline is a normal answer producing PaymentDeclined, which cancels the order and releases stock. A timeout or 5xx is an error: the handler throws and goes through retry, then the DLQ.
haiku-low.q9: PaymentDeclined causes the release. Inventory releases the reservation, if it is RESERVED, setting it to RELEASED and restoring stock. Order Service cancels the order on that same event, not the release.
haiku-low.q10: Order Service consumes StockRejected, PaymentSucceeded and PaymentDeclined. In one transaction it sets status from PENDING to CONFIRMED or CANCELLED, records processed_events, and writes an OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled outbox row.
haiku-low.q11: Notification's consumption of OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled, after the status commit, triggers the email. A failed send is logged with no retry and never changes the order status.
haiku-low.q12: Four attempts: immediately, then after 1 s, 10 s and 60 s. After the fourth failure the message goes to the group's DLQ, on-call is paged, the consumer moves on, and the order keeps its status.

sonnet.q1: In one transaction Order Service writes an `orders` row (status PENDING, with customer email and requestId) and an `OrderPlaced` outbox row. It then returns `202 Accepted` with the orderId. The handler never talks to the broker.
sonnet.q2: The relay marks a row sent only after the broker acknowledges the publish. If it dies between the ack and the mark, the row is sent again on the next poll (every 500 ms). Delivery is at-least-once, and consumers dedupe.
sonnet.q3: The single topic `order-events` is keyed by `orderId`, so one order's events stay in one partition. Each consumer group gets one order's events in published order. The broker gives each partition to one instance of the group, so one instance at a time handles an order.
sonnet.q4: Only a `StockReserved` event triggers a charge. Inventory emits `StockReserved` only when stock was reserved (it emits `StockRejected` otherwise), and Payment charges on nothing else. The charge uses key `charge:{orderId}`. If there is no payment_requests row, the handler throws and no charge is made.
sonnet.q5: They write the result event to their own outbox table in the same transaction as the state change. Their relay then publishes it to `order-events`, keyed by orderId. If one crashes after the commit but before publishing, the outbox row is already saved, so the relay publishes it later. If the crash happens before the commit, nothing is saved.
sonnet.q6: Each consumer inserts the `eventId` into `processed_events` (primary key) in the same transaction as its work. A duplicate hits the unique key, so it changes nothing, writes no outbox row and acks. A second guard on the business key covers the same event under a new eventId: one reservation and one payment per orderId, and status changes only from PENDING. Notification also has a unique email_log key on (orderId, type).
sonnet.q7: Payment sends the same idempotency key `charge:{orderId}` on every attempt. The key comes from the order, not the event. The provider returns the first result and does not charge again. The crash rolled back the transaction, so the handler reruns and gets that result. This only holds while the provider remembers the key, and its retention window is an open question.
sonnet.q8: A decline is a normal answer. Payment writes a DECLINED payments row and a `PaymentDeclined` outbox event, which cancels the order and releases the stock. A timeout or 5xx is an error. The handler throws, the transaction rolls back and nothing is written. It then goes through retry (1 s, 10 s, 60 s) and the DLQ, and the order stays PENDING.
sonnet.q9: The `PaymentDeclined` event causes the release. The Inventory service consumes it and, if the reservation is RESERVED, sets it to RELEASED and restores stock in one transaction. If it is already RELEASED or missing, it only inserts processed_events and acks.
sonnet.q10: It consumes `StockRejected`, `PaymentSucceeded` and `PaymentDeclined` events. In one transaction it updates orders.status from PENDING to CONFIRMED (on PaymentSucceeded) or CANCELLED (on StockRejected or PaymentDeclined). It also inserts processed_events and writes an `OrderConfirmed` or `OrderCancelled` outbox row.
sonnet.q11: Notification consumes `OrderConfirmed` or `OrderCancelled`, which Order Service publishes after the status commit. It claims an email_log row and processed_events, commits, and then sends the email. If the send fails, it logs it and returns normally, with no retry and no DLQ entry. The order status is never changed.
sonnet.q12: Four attempts: the first at once, then retries after 1 s, 10 s and 60 s. If the fourth fails, the message goes to that group's DLQ and on-call is paged. The consumer commits its offset past it and moves on. Nothing is undone, so the order keeps whatever status it had (e.g. PENDING with stock held).
